title: Leadership, prioritising and delegation
blurb: Prioritise women and babies by acuity, delegate safely to maternity support workers under Code 11, and lead by example whatever your band.
question: A postnatal ward midwife is asked to give an intramuscular oxytocin injection by a maternity support worker who offers to do it to save time. What should the midwife do?

teach.body: SPM 5.19 asks midwives to lead and manage midwifery care safely, prioritising, delegating and assigning care to others; SPM 5.20 to show positive leadership and role modelling across the interdisciplinary team. Code 25 asks every registrant to provide leadership to make sure people's wellbeing is protected and their care improved. In plain English: leadership is not a job title. It is how you organise care, share tasks safely and behave when others are watching.

steps.label: Within competence
steps.sub: The task suits their training and skills

teach.caption: NMC Code 11.1–11.3. You stay accountable for the decision to delegate.

rows.label: Delegate because
values: Not to save time or money

teach.caption: RCN delegation guidance and NMC Code 11.

teach.body: The midwives' exemptions in Schedule 17 of the Human Medicines Regulations 2012 let registered midwives, and student midwives under direct supervision, give certain parenteral medicines such as oxytocins without a prescription. They do not extend to maternity support workers. Student midwives may not give diamorphine, morphine or pethidine, even under supervision. So giving IM oxytocin is a task you cannot delegate to a support worker.
teach.cite: Human Medicines Regulations 2012 Sch 17; NMC Code 18

teach.caption: NICE NG4: acuity is the seriousness of a woman's or baby's condition and risk of deterioration.

teach.body: At 08:00 midwife Bea has: Chloe, soaking a pad every 15 minutes; Dami's baby, due a pre-feed glucose; two women awaiting discharge. She goes to Chloe and calls for help. She asks Kim, a maternity support worker trained and assessed in neonatal glucose testing, to do the baby's test and report the result straight back. Discharges wait. Later Bea checks Kim's result and records, and thanks her.

head: Task
To a trained MSW?
rows: IM oxytocin, anti-D, vitamin K injection

teach.body: Students and support workers copy what they see. Show compassion and respect, speak up about poor care, admit uncertainty, give credit, and keep to policies when it would be quicker not to. East Kent named giving care with compassion and kindness and teamworking with a common purpose as areas for action. Challenging a colleague's disrespectful remark about a woman, calmly and privately, is leadership.

teach.text: Delegating a task does not delegate your accountability for deciding to delegate it. And delegation is for the woman's benefit and within the other person's competence, not to save time.

items: Code 11: delegate within the other person's competence, make sure they understand, supervise and confirm the outcome.
The midwife is accountable for the decision to delegate; the support worker for carrying it out, and may decline.
Midwives' medicine exemptions do not extend to maternity support workers; students cannot give diamorphine, morphine or pethidine.
Prioritise by acuity: life-threatening first, routine tasks last.
Leadership is for every midwife: role model compassion, challenge poor care, support the team.

summary: You can now prioritise care by acuity and delegate safely within Code 11, knowing which tasks cannot be delegated. You can also lead and role model positively in the interdisciplinary team whatever your role.

A.q: According to Code 11.1, which tasks may a midwife delegate?
options: Tasks the midwife is too busy to do
Tasks within the other person's competence
Tasks the support worker volunteers for
Tasks listed in the support worker's job title
A.why: Code 11.1: only delegate tasks and duties that are within the other person's scope of competence, making sure they fully understand your instructions.

whyNot.0: Workload is not a basis for delegation; competence is.
whyNot.3: A job title does not confirm the individual's competence.

A.q: A midwife delegates postnatal observations to a trained maternity support worker. Who is accountable for the decision to delegate?
options: The support worker
The ward manager
The midwife
The trust
A.why: The midwife who delegates stays accountable for the decision to delegate; the support worker is accountable for carrying out the task.

whyNot.0: The support worker is accountable for performing the task, not for the decision.
whyNot.1: The ward manager did not make this decision.
whyNot.3: Professional accountability for the decision rests with the midwife who made it.

A.q: A postnatal midwife has four tasks. Which should she attend to first?
options: A woman soaking a pad every 15 minutes
A woman waiting to be discharged home
A baby due a routine weight check
A woman asking for help with expressing
A.why: Prioritise by acuity: heavy postpartum bleeding is potentially life-threatening.

whyNot.1: Discharge is routine and can wait.
whyNot.2: A routine weight is not urgent.
whyNot.3: Feeding support matters but is not life-threatening.

B.q: A maternity support worker is asked to record newborn observations but says she has not been trained or assessed in this. What should happen?
options: She does it under the midwife's name
She watches a video and starts at once
She does it and the midwife countersigns
She declines and the midwife does it
B.why: Code 11.1: delegate only within competence. A person who is not trained should decline, and the midwife carries out the task until training and assessment are complete.

whyNot.0: Working under another's name does not provide competence.
whyNot.1: A video is not training and assessment of competence.
whyNot.2: Countersigning does not make an untrained person competent.

B.q: A busy midwife wants to delegate a task to a support worker. Which reason for delegating is appropriate?
options: It will let her catch up on her notes
The support worker is quicker at this task
It helps the woman and is within competence
It reduces the overall cost of care
B.why: RCN delegation guidance: delegate in the patient's interest and within the person's competence, not to save time or money.

whyNot.0: Saving the midwife time is not, on its own, a valid reason.
whyNot.1: Speed is not the test; competence and the woman's interest are.
whyNot.3: Delegation is not done to save money.

B.q: A maternity support worker offers to give a woman's IM oxytocin for the third stage while the midwife supports the baby. What should the midwife do?
options: Accept, as she has watched it many times
Give the oxytocin herself
Accept, with the midwife watching
Ask the woman to consent first
B.why: HMR 2012 Sch 17 exemptions cover registered midwives and student midwives under supervision, not maternity support workers. The midwife gives it herself.

whyNot.0: Watching is not authorisation; the exemption does not cover MSWs.
whyNot.2: Supervision does not extend the midwives' exemption to MSWs.
whyNot.3: Consent cannot authorise an MSW to give this medicine.

C.q: A midwife asks a trained support worker to check a baby's pre-feed blood glucose. What is the midwife's remaining responsibility?
options: None, once the task is handed over
Repeat the test herself to check it
Ensure the result is reported and acted on
Record the result under her own name
C.why: Code 11.3: confirm that the outcome of any delegated task meets the required standard; the midwife makes sure the result comes back and is acted on.

whyNot.0: The midwife keeps responsibility for supervising and confirming the outcome.
whyNot.1: Repeating every test is unnecessary if the support worker is competent.
whyNot.3: The person who did the test records it.

C.q: During handover a midwife hears a colleague call a woman 'difficult' in front of a student. What is the best example of positive role modelling?
options: Stay silent to keep handover running smoothly
Agree, to keep good relations with her
Report the colleague to the NMC
Challenge it calmly and explain her needs
C.why: SPM 5.20 and East Kent: model compassion and kindness; challenging disrespectful language calmly shows the student how to advocate for women.

whyNot.0: Staying silent teaches the student that disrespect is acceptable.
whyNot.2: A single remark is dealt with locally, not by the regulator.

C.q: A labour ward coordinator has one experienced midwife and one newly qualified midwife free. A woman on magnesium sulfate for severe pre-eclampsia and a low-risk woman in early labour need care. How should she allocate them?
options: Experienced midwife to the woman with pre-eclampsia
Newly qualified midwife to the woman with pre-eclampsia
Both midwives to the woman with pre-eclampsia
Allocate by who has the fewest hours worked
C.why: Match skill mix to acuity: the experienced midwife takes the high-acuity woman; the newly qualified midwife cares for the low-risk woman with support available.

whyNot.1: The higher acuity woman needs the more experienced midwife.
whyNot.2: Leaving the other woman without a midwife is unsafe.
whyNot.3: Hours worked are not a basis for matching skills to need.

reteach.title: Right task, right person, right check
reteach.question: What three checks make delegation safe?

blocks.body: Right task: is it something that can be delegated, and not a medicine under the midwives' exemptions or a clinical judgement? Right person: are they trained and assessed, and do they understand? Right check: do you supervise and confirm the outcome? You stay accountable for the decision; they are accountable for doing it.

blocks.text: A support worker's willingness or experience of watching is not competence.

explain.body: Make sure everyone you delegate tasks to is adequately supervised and supported so they can provide safe and compassionate care, and that they understand your instructions.

test.q: Before a support worker starts a delegated task, what must the midwife make sure of?
options: That the task is quick
That a student is present
That the woman has been discharged
That they understand the instructions
test.why: Code 11.1–11.2: make sure the person fully understands your instructions and is supervised and supported.

whyNot.0: Speed is not a requirement of delegation.
whyNot.1: A student's presence does not ensure understanding.
whyNot.2: Delegation does not depend on discharge.

explain.body: Code 25: all registrants have opportunities to show leadership regardless of formal position; 25.1 identify priorities and manage time, staff and resources, putting the needs of those receiving care first.

items.label: support staff to follow the Code

test.q: According to the NMC Code, who is expected to show leadership?
options: Every registrant, whatever their role
Band 7 midwives and above
The head of midwifery
Midwives with a leadership qualification
test.why: Code 25: all registrants have opportunities to show leadership regardless of formal position.

whyNot.1: Leadership is not limited to senior bands.
whyNot.2: The head of midwifery leads, but so does every midwife.
whyNot.3: No qualification is needed to show leadership.

explain.body: NG4: acuity is the seriousness of a woman's or baby's condition and the risk of deterioration; dependency is how much she depends on direct care for daily needs.

rows.label: Means
values: Need for help with daily care

test.q: In NICE NG4, what does 'acuity' describe?
options: The number of women on the ward at once
The help a woman needs with personal care
How unwell she is and her risk of deteriorating
The experience of the staff on duty today
test.why: NG4: acuity refers to the seriousness of a woman's or baby's condition, the risk of clinical deterioration and their specific care needs.

whyNot.1: Help with personal care is dependency.

explain.body: Student midwives may give the Sch 17 parenteral medicines under the direct supervision of a registered midwife, except diamorphine, morphine and pethidine.

test.q: Which medicine may a student midwife NOT give under the midwives' exemptions, even under direct supervision?
options: Oxytocin
Pethidine
Anti-D immunoglobulin
Phytomenadione
test.why: HMR 2012 Sch 17: student midwives are excluded from diamorphine, morphine and pethidine.

whyNot.0: Oxytocins are allowed for students under direct supervision.
whyNot.2: Anti-D is allowed for students under direct supervision.
whyNot.3: Phytomenadione is allowed for students under direct supervision.
